What I checked:
- `TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd` now builds a real `*daemon.PipelineStore{Dir: storeDir, ...}` and passes it as `NewMailHandler`'s final argument, matching the production shape in `cmd/beadle-daemon/main.go:65-68` and the signature in `internal/daemon/handler.go:58`.
- The new assertion block (harness_test.go:165-181) reads `storeDir` after `handler.Stop()` and checks exactly one JSON record exists with `Status == "completed"` and `Email.From == "[redacted-email]"` for the positive case, and an empty directory for both negative gate cases (unsigned message, `rw-` permission).
- Traced the happens-before chain: `Executor.Run` (pipeline.go:213-215) calls `e.save(p)` with the final `"completed"` status as its last action before returning; the goroutine's deferred `wg.Done()` (handler.go:189) runs strictly after that in program order; `Stop()`'s `wg.Wait()` (handler.go:86-89) then can't return until `Done()` fires. So reading `storeDir` right after `Stop()` returns is race-free — no sleep/poll needed, consistent with this tier's no-sleep convention.
- Negative cases (gate 1: unsigned message, gate 2: `rw-` contact) are rejected inside `OnNewMail`'s loop (handler.go:150-166) *before* the goroutine/Executor is ever spawned, so the store directory is correctly asserted empty rather than vacuously passing.
- `test-command`'s `Mode: "passthrough"` with no `"reply"` command registered means the pipeline completes without the auto-reply path firing, consistent with expecting exactly one spawner call and one persisted record.
- `storeDir`, `commandsDir`, and `templates.TmpDir` are three independent `t.TempDir()`s, so no cross-contamination of the directory-entry count assertion.
- Matches the mission's stated intent (beadle-fbhp: tie persistence assertion to the pipeline having actually run, so it can't pass vacuously).

No bugs, no convention violations (go.md: table-driven test, require/assert used correctly, t.TempDir(), no panics, no suppressed errors). tool_input.body:
## Summary

Bead **beadle-5ma**. `release.yml` built and uploaded only `beadle-email`; `cmd/beadle-daemon` shipped in no release, so a user had to build it from source. This mirrors the existing loop for the daemon binary in both the CI workflow and `make dist`, so the two produce identical eight-binary asset sets, and hardens the upload step with `fail_on_unmatched_files: true` so an empty glob fails instead of being skipped.

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: second `go build` line inside the existing os/arch loop; checksums cover `beadle-email-* beadle-daemon-*`; `files:` glob adds `dist/beadle-daemon-*`; `fail_on_unmatched_files: true`.
- `Makefile` `dist`: four more cross-compiles, all eight named in `checksums.txt`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Added entry under Unreleased.
- Mission exports m-2026-10-22-016 and -024 (paths redacted).

Scope note: `install.sh` and the README install flow still install `beadle-email` only, by design; a daemon installer is separate scope.

## Demo

Expected: `make dist` produces eight binaries plus `checksums.txt`; the native linux-amd64 daemon runs; version is injected; checksums verify; workflow lints clean.

```text
$ ls dist
beadle-daemon-darwin-amd64  beadle-daemon-darwin-arm64  beadle-daemon-linux-amd64  beadle-daemon-linux-arm64
beadle-email-darwin-amd64   beadle-email-darwin-arm64   beadle-email-linux-amd64   beadle-email-linux-arm64
checksums.txt

$ dist/beadle-daemon-linux-amd64 --help
beadle-daemon: background daemon for Beadle
Usage:
  beadle-daemon [command]
Available Commands:
  completion  init  run  sign  verify  help

$ dist/beadle-email-linux-amd64 version
beadle-email 0.16.5-28-gfbe4244

$ file dist/beadle-daemon-linux-arm64
ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, statically linked, stripped
$ file dist/beadle-daemon-darwin-arm64
Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable

$ (cd dist && sha256sum -c checksums.txt)   # evaluator-run
all 8: OK

$ actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml
(no output)
$ shellcheck <extracted build step>
(no output)
```

Missing-dependency case: `sha256sum beadle-email-* beadle-daemon-*` with a missing binary exits 1 on the literal glob (reviewer-reproduced), and the Makefile recipe stops at the first failed build line. Boundary: with only email binaries present the checksum step still exits 1 for the daemon glob.

Operator confirmation: the release itself runs only on a `v*` tag push, so the live upload is confirmed at the next release rather than here. Everything that can run locally ran locally.

## Gate

Worktree `make check` stopped at `lint-strict` on the six known gosec G204 lines in untouched files (the worktree relative-path artifact; diff touches no Go and no `.golangci.yml`). `vet`, `staticcheck`, `lint-shell`, `vulncheck`, `docs`, and the full `-race` test suite were run explicitly and are green. Evaluator (rsc) accept with zero findings; code-reviewer and silent-failure-hunter clean; one hardening from the latter landed as `bef1039`.

tool_input.message:
Round-4 re-verification of the poll-interval "cannot drift" claim at 38a061f. Verdict: the in-binary claim is now structurally true. The inbox.md doc test's claim is wider than what it enforces, and one of those gaps is a real behavioral drift path (HIGH). Everything below was checked by mutating scratch copies of the module under .tmp/ and running `go test -race` on them; the repo tree was not edited and the scratch copies are deleted.

== In-binary derivation: CONFIRMED ==
Every interval string compiled into the binary derives from validPollIntervals (internal/email/config.go:182) via PollIntervals()/PollIntervalList() (internal/email/poller.go:28, :49):
- internal/email/poller.go:138 Start() config error
- internal/email/poller.go:350 InvalidIntervalError.Error()
- internal/mcp/poll_tools.go:30 both the tool description and the "interval" param description
- internal/mcp/poll_tools.go:127 handler error
No literal interval list remains in non-test Go. One literal list remains in a Go *comment*: config.go:205 ("Valid values: "1m", "2m", ... "2h", "n", """) restates the map it sits next to; nothing catches it going stale. LOW; replace with "Valid values: the keys of validPollIntervals plus "n" and """.

== Mutation results ==
A) Add an unused "20m" to the map. Failed: TestPollIntervals_SortedAscending (pin), TestInboxDoc_ListsFullIntervalSet. Passed: all three poll_tools_test "FullSet" tests, TestPollDuration, TestValidPollInterval.
B) Add "4m" (the invalid fixture) to the map. Failed: TestPollDuration, TestValidPollInterval, TestPoller_SetInterval_Invalid, TestPoller_Start_InvalidPollIntervalNamesFullSet, TestPollIntervals_SortedAscending, TestHandler_SetPollInterval_Invalid, TestInboxDoc_ListsFullIntervalSet. Passed: the three poll_tools_test FullSet tests.
C) inbox.md: change the 15m cron row to `*/5 * * * *`. TestInboxDoc PASSES.
D) Remove "15m" from the map. Failed: TestPollDuration, TestPollIntervals_SortedAscending. The whole internal/mcp suite PASSES, including TestInboxDoc, with 15m still advertised in inbox.md.
E) inbox.md: delete 2m and 3m from the routing list (line 20) and the section heading (line 26), leaving the argument-hint and cron table intact. TestInboxDoc PASSES.

== Per-test reading ==
- TestSetPollInterval_AcceptsEveryValidInterval (poll_tools_test.go:253), TestSetPollInterval_InvalidErrorListsFullSet (:271), TestSetPollIntervalTool_DescriptionsListFullSet (:289): all three iterate PollIntervals() against strings that are themselves built from PollIntervalList(). They cannot fail on a map change (A and B confirm). What they genuinely guard is a *regression* to a hand-typed literal in poll_tools.go that later goes stale. That is a legitimate purpose and matches their comments; just be aware they are not the thing that fires when someone adds a value. Fine as-is.
- TestPollIntervals_SortedAscending (poller_test.go:214): a pinned literal list. It does prove ordering for real (appending "20m" to the pin in the wrong position fails, since PollIntervals() sorts by duration), and it is the only Go test that fires on a generic addition, so it doubles as the acknowledge-the-change gate. Acceptable. A derived form (assert validPollIntervals[names[i]] < validPollIntervals[names[i+1]] and len equality) would drop the pin without losing the ordering check, but there is no false claim here.
- poller_test.go:60 and :206, poll_tools_test.go:281, :330, :331: derived loops, correct direction. See MEDIUM-2 for a substring weakness they share.
- TestInboxDoc_ListsFullIntervalSet (poll_tools_test.go:338): see findings below.
- TestPollDuration / TestValidPollInterval (config_test.go:63, :96): hand-pinned snapshots; they make no drift claim, so not a finding, but note they are silent on a new value (A) and are the ones that fire on removal (D).

== Findings ==

HIGH-1. Claim: "TestInboxDoc_ListsFullIntervalSet proves plugin/commands/inbox.md cannot drift from email.PollIntervals()" (poll_tools_test.go:335-337). inbox.md carries the set FOUR times: argument-hint (line 3), the routing rule (line 20, "Exactly one of ... → set polling interval"), the section heading (line 26), and the cron table (lines 44-46). The test checks only line 3 (`| v |`) and the cron table (`` `v` → ``). Falsifying case (E, confirmed): add "20m" to the map, add it to the argument-hint and cron table because the test told you to, skip line 20 because the test went green. The agent executing /inbox then routes `/inbox 20m` as a *filter query* per line 20/24, never calls set_poll_interval, never creates the cron. That is exactly the user-facing drift the test claims to prevent. Fix (preferred): collapse the copies. Make line 20 and line 26 refer to the cron table ("exactly one of the intervals in the cron table under step 3") so the set appears in two places, both of which the test already checks. Fix (minimal): add a third Contains check for "`"+interval+"`" within the line that starts with "- Exactly one of".

MEDIUM-2. Same claim, other direction. The test asserts map ⊆ doc, never doc ⊆ map. Falsifying case (D, confirmed): remove "15m" from the map; mcp suite green; inbox.md still offers 15m in all four places, and the agent gets an error from set_poll_interval on a value the command's own hint advertised. Fix: parse the argument-hint tokens between "[" and "]" (split on " | ", drop "<filter text>", "n", "status") and the cron-table keys, and assert.ElementsMatch each against PollIntervals(). That turns the check into set equality, and it also catches a cron row for a value that no longer exists.

MEDIUM-3. Cron-row strictness. The `` `v` → `` check proves a row exists, not that its expression is right (C, confirmed: `15m` → `*/5 * * * *` passes). The test's own comment only promises "a cron-expression row", so the claim is narrow and met; but the expression is what actually drives polling cadence in Claude Code, and a wrong row means the MCP poller and the /inbox cron tick at different rates with nothing to flag it. The durations are already in validPollIntervals, so the expected expression is derivable: minutes < 60 → "*/N * * * *"; 1h → "0 * * * *"; N hours → "0 */N * * *". Recommend asserting the full row text "`v` → `expr`" from that derivation; a newly added value then gets its row content checked automatically, not just its presence. Only worth doing if you are touching the test for HIGH-1 anyway; on its own it is a correctness-of-doc check, not a drift check.

MEDIUM-4. Substring masking in the five derived Contains loops (poller_test.go:61, :207; poll_tools_test.go:281, :330, :331). "5m" is a substring of "15m", so a string that lost 5m but kept 15m satisfies assert.Contains(text, "5m"). Today harmless because the strings derive; it only matters on a regression to a literal, which is precisely the case these tests exist for. Fix: in the error-text tests, strings.Split the "rest" on ", " after trimming ", or n" and assert.ElementsMatch against PollIntervals(); in the description test, same on the substring between "Valid intervals: " and ". Use 'n'". The inbox.md test is immune because it brackets each value with "| " / "`".

== Hand-maintained copies that remain ==
- README.md:140 and :150 (tool table, slash-command table). User-facing, same drift class that bit last round, zero enforcement. Cheap to add to TestInboxDoc's pattern (one more ReadFile, assert each PollIntervals() value is in both lines). Recommend doing it; it is the surface a new user reads first.
- DESIGN.md:504 ("valid: 1m, 2m, ... n"). Design narrative; acceptable hand-maintained, or reword to "the keys of validPollIntervals" so it cannot go stale.
- CHANGELOG.md:57 and earlier entries: historical by nature, correct to leave.
- config.go:205 comment (LOW, above).

Net: the structural fix for the binary is real and complete. The doc guard is the piece whose comment overstates it; HIGH-1 is the one I would not merge past, MEDIUM-2 is a five-line change that also subsumes most of the value of MEDIUM-3.

tool_input.message:
Re-review of b6981f3..06115c9 (hardened registry exec test). Three of the five fixes close their gap. The install-remedy fix introduced a worse defect, and the "usage" match and the kill path each leave a narrower hole. Details with file:line below. I ran the tests in the worktree and the real binaries on this host; I did not edit anything.

CRITICAL — the remedy names make targets that do not exist, and the comment claims provisioning that nothing on the branch does.
Location: internal/daemon/templates_test.go:163-168 (doc comment) and :216-227 (mcpCommandInstallRemedy).
The comment says "All three of today's stdio entries are provisioned by `make test`: ... beadle-email via the tools-beadle-email target ... biff via the tools-biff target; CI adds GOPATH/bin ... and the build output directory to PATH". None of that is true at 06115c9:
- `git grep tools-beadle-email|tools-biff` over the whole tree at 06115c9 hits only the test file itself.
- Makefile at 06115c9 has only `tools-ethos`; `test: tools-ethos`. No beadle-email self-build onto PATH, no biff install.
- .github/workflows/test.yml installs ethos only and adds only GOPATH/bin. `git diff main..06115c9 --stat -- Makefile .github/` is empty: the branch never touched either.
Consequence: on a clean CI runner, `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal/beadle-email` and `/biff` fail at exec.LookPath, and the failure message tells the reader to run a make target that returns "No rule to make target". The test passes here only because ~/.local/bin already has all three (beadle-email 0.16.5, ethos 4.19.1, biff). Note also that the beadle-email subtest therefore exercises the previously installed 0.16.5 binary, not ./cmd/beadle-email on this branch, so "a self-build of ./cmd/beadle-email" is also false and the subtest says nothing about the branch's own serve command. Finding 5's original complaint (ethos-only remedy) has been replaced by a confidently wrong remedy, and the real gap (no provisioning for two of three commands) is still open and is now hidden behind prose asserting it is closed.
Fix: either add real `tools-beadle-email` (go build -o $(GOINSTALL_BIN)/beadle-email ./cmd/beadle-email) and `tools-biff` targets, wire them into `test:`, and add matching CI steps, or drop beadle-email and biff from the exec test and say so. Either way the comment must describe what the Makefile and CI actually do.

HIGH — default branch "install it" lets a new registry entry ship with no provisioning story.
Location: internal/daemon/templates_test.go:225-226.
A future `"foo": {Command: "foo"}` entry passes locally if foo happens to be installed and fails in CI with the useless remedy "install it". The remedy table is a parallel copy of the registry with no check that the two agree. Recommend: make an unknown command a failure in its own right, independent of LookPath, so adding a registry entry forces adding its make target and remedy case:
```go
remedy, ok := mcpCommandInstallRemedy(cfg.Command)
require.True(t, ok, "registry entry %q names command %q with no provisioning story: add a Makefile tools-%s target, a CI step, and a case in mcpCommandInstallRemedy", name, cfg.Command, cfg.Command)
```
and drop the `default: return "install it"` arm.

MEDIUM — the "usage" check is looser than it needs to be and misses the original defect class on a different kind of binary.
Location: internal/daemon/templates_test.go:202.
`strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(out), "usage")` runs only after exit 0 and no timeout, so cobra's and Click's unknown-command errors (both non-zero; I confirmed `ethos mcp --help` exits 2 with `unknown command "mcp"` and no usage text) are caught earlier. But two things slip through: (a) a server whose startup log contains the word in any case, e.g. a `msg="disk usage ..."` slog line, satisfies it after stdin EOF; (b) a binary whose unknown-subcommand handler prints root usage and exits 0 passes even though the registry's Args name a subcommand that does not exist, which is exactly the ethos "mcp" defect this test was written for. All three real outputs contain the literal `Usage:` followed by the full command line (`ethos serve [flags]`, `beadle-email serve [flags]`, ` Usage: biff mcp [OPTIONS]`). Recommend requiring `Usage:` case-sensitive and the configured subcommand on the same output:
```go
want := cfg.Command + " " + strings.Join(cfg.Args, " ")
if !strings.Contains(string(out), "Usage:") || !strings.Contains(string(out), want) {
```

MEDIUM — the 5s deadline bounds the kill, not the return; a started server that forks can hang the test past the deadline.
Location: internal/daemon/templates_test.go:184-187.
exec.CommandContext kills the direct child at the deadline, but CombinedOutput also waits for the stdout/stderr pipes to close. If a swallowed --help starts a server that spawns a child inheriting those pipes (biff mcp's local relay is the plausible case; beadle-email serve on stdin EOF actually dialed the live mailbox on this host before exiting), the kill lands and CombinedOutput still blocks until go test's own package timeout fires, with no per-entry message. Set `cmd.WaitDelay = time.Second` (Go 1.20+) so the pipes are abandoned shortly after the kill and the ctx.Err() branch at :188 actually runs.

Confirmed closed, no new silent path:
- ctx.Err() ordering (:188-190): checked before `err` is inspected, so DeadlineExceeded wins whether CombinedOutput surfaced it as an ExitError(-1) or as the context error. The only race is a process that exits non-zero in the same instant the deadline fires being reported as a timeout, which is still a failure, not a pass.
- exercised counter (:177 before :178): incremented in the parent loop before t.Run, so a Fatalf inside the subtest still counts and require.Greater at :207 sees it. An all-http registry now fails at :207. The parent-level require.NoError at :173 aborts on the first malformed entry before later entries run, which is loud, not silent.
- Validate before skip (:173-176): an entry with nothing set fails Validate ("sets neither stdio fields nor http fields"), so `Command == ""` is only reached by a shape Validate accepted as http. Closed.
- cmd/beadle-email/admin_cmd.go:39 `Args: cobra.NoArgs` and the test at admin_cmd_test.go:342-346: ValidateArgs runs before RunE, confirmed by the test reaching the error with no server started; the error contains "bogus". Closed. (PersistentPreRun sets SilenceUsage after ValidateArgs, so the stray-arg error prints the full usage block; noise, not a hiding path.)

Verification run: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestDefaultMCPRegistry|TestServeCmd_RejectsStrayPositional' -v ./internal/daemon/ ./cmd/beadle-email/` in the mcp-serve worktree: all pass on this host, for the reason stated in the CRITICAL finding.
